title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the Committee’s 2020 report on AI and public standards lays out its commitment to creating clear guidelines and oversight for AI technologies. It stresses collaboration with industry, research bodies and international partners to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent and aligned with public values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual will set clear rules to make sure artificial intelligence is used fairly and transparently in exams, tests and other qualifications, protecting students, teachers and the integrity of assessment. They plan to create guidelines that prevent cheating, ensure reliability, and keep AI tools from giving an unfair advantage, while working closely with education, science, innovation and business officials to keep the system up‑to‑date.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted works and evaluates the legal and economic effects of that use. It offers guidance for balancing the protection of creators’ rights with the need to foster innovation in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, outlining actions to address concerns about AI’s impact on society, the economy, and national security. It emphasizes the need for stronger regulation, investment in research, and international cooperation to keep the UK at the forefront of AI development while safeguarding public interests.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the goals, scope, and duties of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence interacts with public standards, including a FAQ section to help stakeholders understand the process. It outlines the review framework, key timelines, and expected outcomes so that AI practices can be aligned with public expectations and regulatory requirements.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely outlines the organisation’s views on how AI should be regulated and overseen, although specific details are not included here.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how AI technologies will shape the rules and standards for medical products, ensuring they remain safe, effective, and trustworthy. It adopts the principles from the AI White Paper to guide regulators, manufacturers, and stakeholders in integrating AI while maintaining transparency, accountability, and compliance with existing health regulations.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organization the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence force for its size. It focuses on developing and deploying advanced AI technologies to enhance operational capabilities, decision‑making, and strategic influence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to make the most of AI benefits while also controlling possible risks. It outlines steps to develop AI responsibly and supports industry uptake.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report details how copyright‑protected works are being used to train AI systems, outlining current practices, challenges, and the legal framework under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights progress made, identifies gaps, and recommends actions to align AI development with copyright law while fostering innovation.
